title: Prompt + Quantization runbook (daybook)
content:
Daily log (fast-moving, messy)

2026-02-28 — kickoff
- Goal: get a stable prompt harness for the 7B finetuned family and baseline FP16 runs + 4-bit quantized runs. Compare latency and generation quality on the user-sim dataset (50 short dialogues).
- Quick plan: build harness, run 20 samples with seed control, collect logits perplexity-ish metric + human-oriented pass/fail (answer correct?).

Morning checklist
- [x] scaffold prompt harness (local python script)
- [x] add deterministic seeding and token-level logging
- [x] add warmup steps in runner to normalize kernel selection
- [ ] sanity-check dataset for label noise

Experimental notes (commands)
- Baseline: python run_eval.py --model ./models/finetuned-7b/ --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seed 42 --out results/fp16-02-28.json
- Q4 (GPTQ 4-bit, per-channel): python run_eval.py --model ./models/finetuned-7b/ --quant gptq --bits 4 --group-size 128 --batch 1 --seed 42 --out results/gptq4-02-28.json
- Quick perf probe: ./bin/bench_infer --model models/finetuned-7b/ --dtype int4 --seq 128 --threads 4

First-pass observations
- FP16: latency median ~92ms/sample (local dev box, A100-sim); answers generally coherent, hallucination low on facts in our small dataset.
- GPTQ-4: latency median ~58ms/sample; occasional broken tokens at end of outputs (truncated words) — maybe group-size or rocm kernel mismatch.
- Perplexity proxy (token-log-loss) increased by ~6% on average for GPTQ4 vs FP16. However human pass/fail only down by 4/50 samples.

Hypotheses
1) Token truncation correlates with prompt length + greedy sampling; try temperature=0.7 vs 0.0 to see decoding stability.
2) Group size=128 might be too coarse; test 64 and 32 for GPTQ-4 to check artifact frequency.
3) KV-cache alignment in quant path may cause tail-emission issues when sequence length > 180.

Immediate TODOs (priority)
- [ ] Run GPTQ-4 with group-size 64 and 32 (r1)
- [ ] Re-run with temp=0.0 and top_p=0.95 to isolate sampling noise (r2)
- [ ] Add token-level diffs to runner to capture where truncation occurs (prefix length, token id)
- [ ] Validate that ONNX/compilation step preserved eos token ID mapping (r3)

Run matrix (notes to self)
- r1: q4-gs128, q4-gs64, q4-gs32 (same seed)
- r2: fp16-temp0.0, fp16-temp0.7, q4-temp0.0, q4-temp0.7
- r3: seq120 vs seq256 on a few long prompts (look for KV misalignment)

Representative prompts/test cases
- T1: "You are a helpful assistant. Q: How to reset a Git repo to a previous commit? A:" (precise procedural answer expected)
- T2: "Summarize the following short chat between customer and agent about billing disputes." (expected concise summary)
- T3: edge-case: long context with code snippet, expects correct code continuation (sensitive to truncation)

Scratch experiment results (notes, raw)
- results/fp16-02-28.json: mean_token_loss: 1.82, median_latency_ms: 92, human_pass: 46/50
- results/gptq4-02-28.json: mean_token_loss: 1.93, median_latency_ms: 58, human_pass: 42/50, trunc_errors: 6
- quick-bench logs: int4 kernel fallback observed at iteration 3 on the dev box (stack trace in bench.log)

Manual triage steps (what I tried)
- Recompiled model with per-channel symmetric quant and small calibration set (100 samples) — truncation persisted.
- Re-ran with different tokenizer version (v2.1 -> v2.0) — no change.
- Verified eos token id in model config: matches tokenizer.

Questions to follow up in sync w/ SRE and runtime team
- Does the serving runtime alter last-token emission ordering for quantized kernels? (cc @Riley Chen)
- Are there known issues with group-size power-of-two constraints on the new int4 kernels? (cc @Samir Patel)

Notes for triage doc / PR text
- Short blurb for PR: "Empirical: 7B finetuned family shows 4-bit GPTQ reduces latency ~35-40% at small cost to token-loss and a small increase in truncation events for long-context prompts. Recommend controlled rollout behind routing policy and user-visible degrade flag."

Future experiments (week roadmap)
- Sweep quantization: GPTQ 3-bit (if available) vs 4-bit, per-channel vs per-tensor
- Measure cost-per-100k tokens on dedicated infra to estimate RU impact for Dedicated customers
- Add automated unit tests in harness that assert no truncation on our long-context sample set

Random scratch thoughts (notes-to-self)
- Might be worth instrumenting prefix-cache hits in the harness to reproduce cache/warmup behavior found in prod.
- Could use small human-eval cohort (5 reviewers) for qualitative scoring rather than binary pass/fail.

End-of-day micro-retrospective (2026-02-28)
- Wins: harness up, baseline runs done, clear candidate config to test next.
- Pain: flaky int4 kernel fallback on local dev — open bug.
- Next: run r1 and r2 early AM, shell out brief update to applied-ml channel after r1 completes.

-- Elena
